summary: Episode 42 closes the Isra' Mi'raj section. The ustaz begins with a hadith of Abu Hurairah RA: whoever makes worship the centre of his life, Allah fills his heart with contentment, and whoever does not, Allah fills his hands with busyness. He links prayer to provision, family and the loneliness crisis of modern people, then walks through the nine kinds of disconnection in the book Lost Connections and shows how Islam's teachings protect each connection: meaningful work, human relationships, values, small traumas, respect, nature and a hopeful future. The second part returns to Sidrat al-Muntaha: three gifts to the Prophet ﷺ, the two lights, namely Al-Fatihah and the last two verses of Al-Baqarah, and the supplication that has already been granted.
keyPoints: Hadith of Abu Hurairah RA: make worship the centre of life, and Allah fills the heart with contentment and removes poverty. Otherwise the hands are filled with busyness and never with enough.
Prayer and provision are linked. Allah does not ask us for provision, He is the Provider, so do not abandon prayer or take up forbidden work out of fear for your income.
Salah means both to bend and to supplicate. Prayer is our connection with Allah, and modern people are in a crisis of disconnection.
Of the nine disconnections in Lost Connections, Islam protects each one: meaningful work, human relationships, values, small traumas, respect, nature and hope for the future.
At Sidrat al-Muntaha the Prophet ﷺ was given the five prayers, the last two verses of Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of major sins for those who do not associate partners with Allah.
Al-Fatihah and the last two verses of Al-Baqarah are two lights in the form of supplication, and Allah has answered them.

lessons.title: Make worship the centre of life, and the heart will be filled
lessons.body: Hadith of Abu Hurairah: Allah fills the heart with richness and contentment for those who put worship first. Someone who thinks only of this world will always see what is lacking.

lessons.title: Busy is not the same as productive
lessons.body: Some busy people produce something; others are busy moving left and right in the same place without progress.

lessons.title: Don't abandon prayer or take forbidden work out of fear for provision
lessons.body: Allah says He does not ask us for provision, He is the Provider. Weighing a lucrative job that blocks Friday prayer or involves something forbidden shows we feel provision comes from that job.

lessons.title: The father is the family's example in prayer
lessons.body: If the father himself does not keep prayer, the command to order the family to pray is hard to carry out. Examples at home, such as 'skip Isha because of an exam', shape how children see prayer.

lessons.title: Practise knowledge, don't just collect lectures
lessons.body: In an age of information flood, hearing many lectures only means entering the flood. The measure is whether knowledge is practised and shapes character, like boarding Nuh's ark.

lessons.title: Prayer is the human connection with God
lessons.body: Salah means both supplication and connection. Even a neuroscientist realised people will not find peace until they connect with a 'higher power'.

lessons.title: Look for meaningful work: halal, fits your talent, does no harm
lessons.body: Choosing a career is not only about salary. Meaningless work harms oneself and society. If you can, make your present work meaningful; if not, move on, and trust that Allah looks after provision.

lessons.title: All of life is worship, not only after retirement
lessons.body: The idea of retirement as stopping work comes from the industrial framework, not Islam. The ustaz invites us to ask what our last deed will be.

lessons.title: Keep ties with neighbours, guests, parents and the elderly
lessons.body: Faith is tied to how we treat a hungry neighbour and a guest. The loneliness of abandoned elders shows we should ask why we feel nothing.

lessons.title: Break the cycle of trauma, and don't be the cause of your child's
lessons.body: Prophet Yusuf and Prophet Ibrahim did not surrender to trauma. The Prophet ﷺ never hit or shouted at anyone, and the Quran stresses care for orphans.

lessons.title: Honour all people, and teach children by example
lessons.body: Allah honoured all the children of Adam. How we treat a restaurant waiter or a domestic helper is the most effective lesson for children.

lessons.title: Don't become 'part of the damage'
lessons.body: A person whose heart is alive knows a company that pollutes nature is not meaningful work, and moves on.

lessons.title: Religion gives hope: don't despair, don't obsess over exposing faults
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ did not look for reasons to punish those who confessed. The strict standard of proof protects dignity. Our approach is often the opposite, so that society finds it hard to accept ex-prisoners.

lessons.title: Pray with the supplication Allah taught, and don't be arrogant
lessons.body: The supplication in the last two verses of Al-Baqarah has been answered. It teaches us to admit weakness, forgetfulness and error, and to think collectively about family and the community.

lessons.title: Allah gives direct access with no intermediary
lessons.body: There is no broker, agent or appointment between Allah and His servant. The choice to connect is ours.

glossary.meaning: In the language it means to strike or bend something, and more specifically supplication. Some scholars link it to 'silah', meaning connection.
Connection or relationship, as in silaturrahim.
Young people who shut themselves in and cut off contact with others for years, a phenomenon mentioned in Japan.
The idea that excessive comfort becomes a crisis, because children not trained to face hardship become fragile.
A term for a generation seen as easily fragile. The ustaz studies why it happens.
Staying in the mosque for worship. An example of a time we are cut off from people but not from God.
A gift or talent from Allah. Choosing a career that fits one's mauhibah counts as meaningful work.
Being good to parents, including after their death by keeping ties with their friends and family.
The two lights given to the Prophet ﷺ: Al-Fatihah and the last two verses of Al-Baqarah.
'We hear and we disobey', the words of the People of the Book. The Prophet ﷺ told the Companions to say 'sami'na wa ata'na' (we hear and we obey).

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to another hadith that a person who thinks only of this world will see poverty between his eyes.
dalil.translation: O son of Adam, free yourself for My worship and I will fill your heart with contentment and remove your poverty. If not, I will fill your hands with busyness and not remove your poverty.

dalil.context: The verse about ordering one's family to pray and be patient in it, and that Allah does not ask us for provision. Recited when Umar RA's heart was moved. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Order your people to pray, and pray steadfastly yourself. We are not asking you to give Us provision;We provide for you, and the rewards of the Hereafter belong to the devout.

dalil.context: The ustaz invites us to ask what our last deed will be, relating it to people who stop being meaningful after retirement.
dalil.translation: A person is resurrected in the state of his last deed. One who dies in ihram is resurrected in ihram.

dalil.context: Recited in prayer. The ustaz points out the word 'we', which reminds us to think collectively.
dalil.translation: It is You we worship; it is You we ask for help.

dalil.context: Evidence that faith is tied to connection with other people.
dalil.translation: He does not believe who sleeps with a full stomach while his neighbour goes hungry.

dalil.context: Ties faith to how one treats a guest.
dalil.translation: Whoever believes in the Last Day should honour his guest.

dalil.context: One way of honouring a deceased mother is to honour her sisters.
dalil.translation: The maternal aunt holds the position of the mother.

dalil.context: Islam protects children from trauma, and the Quran repeatedly mentions orphans.
dalil.translation: The wellbeing of Muslim homes depends on how they treat orphans.

dalil.context: Allah honoured all the children of Adam regardless of skin colour, economic background, name or religion. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: We have honoured the children of Adam and carried them by land and sea; We have provided good sustenance for them and favoured them specially above many of those We have created.

dalil.context: Killing one life is like killing all of humanity. The principle of honouring human life. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: On account of [his deed], We decreed to the Children of Israel that if anyone kills a person- unless in retribution for murder or spreading corruption in the land- it is as if he kills all mankind, while if any saves a life it is as if he saves the lives of all mankind. Our messengers came to them with clear signs, but many of them continued to commit excesses in the land.

dalil.context: In the context of honouring people without judging backgrounds that cannot be changed.
dalil.translation: There is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a non-Arab over an Arab.

dalil.context: The Quran tells people to look at their food as part of awareness of nature. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Let man consider the food he eats!

dalil.context: Do not despair of Allah's mercy. The ustaz makes it the basis of a religion that gives hope. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Say, ‘[God says], My servants who have harmed yourselves by your own excess, do not despair of God’s mercy. God forgives all sins: He is truly the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah may forgive or punish first, but such a person does not remain in Hell forever like the disbelievers. The declaration of tawhid is the greatest licence.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ was given the five prayers, the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of major sins for his community who do not associate partners with Allah.

dalil.context: The first of the last two verses of Al-Baqarah, given at Sidrat al-Muntaha.
dalil.translation: The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, as do the faithful. They all believe in God, His angels, His scriptures, and His messengers. ‘We make no distinction between any of His messengers,’ they say, ‘We hear and obey. Grant us Your forgiveness, our Lord. To You we all return!’-

dalil.context: The ustaz reads the translation because of lack of time.
dalil.translation: Jibril heard a sound from above and said this is a door of heaven that has never been opened. An angel descended and greeted: rejoice in two lights never given to any prophet before you, Al-Fatihah and the last two verses of Al-Baqarah. You will not recite a single letter of them except that you will be given what it contains.

dalil.context: Scholars differ on what 'suffice' means: equal to night prayer, protection from the devil's harassment, protection from evil, sufficing as the night's remembrance, or all of these.
dalil.translation: Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him.

dalil.context: In Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman. The ustaz mentions two narrations: one answered 'na'am', the other 'qad fa'alt' (I have done it). The hadith numbers are given as 125 and 126.
dalil.translation: The Companions found verse 284 heavy. The Prophet ﷺ told them to say 'we hear and we obey', not like the People of the Book, 'we hear and we disobey'. After that Allah revealed the last two verses and answered each request.

dalil.context: The verse the Companions found heavy because Allah will account for what is apparent and what is hidden in the heart.
dalil.translation: Whatever is in the heavens and in the earth belongs to God and, whether you reveal or conceal your thoughts, God will call you to account for them. He will forgive whoever He will and punish whoever He will: He has power over all things.

dalil.context: The supplication 'Rabbana la tu'akhidhna...' to which Allah replied 'I have answered'. Allah does not punish for forgetting or erring, and does not burden beyond capacity.
dalil.translation: God does not burden any soul with more than it can bear: each gains whatever good it has done, and suffers its bad- ‘ Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes. Lord, do not burden us as You burdened those before us. Lord, do not burden us with more than we have strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against the disbelievers.’

dalil.context: The ustaz gives the example of missing a prayer time through sleeping or jet lag.
dalil.translation: What is done through forgetfulness, compulsion or sleep is not held against us.
